title: What Is Email Cadence and Why It's Important | Selzy Blog

facts.fact: The Selzy blog article 'What Is Email Cadence and Why It's Important' was published on 27 February 2026.
Selzy's article states that studies suggest starting with 1-3 emails per month as a baseline cadence.
facts.quote: Studies suggest starting with 1-3 emails per month, monitoring engagement before increasing frequency

facts.fact: According to a MailerLite study cited by Selzy, most businesses send between one and three emails monthly.
facts.quote: most businesses send between one and three emails monthly.

facts.fact: According to Litmus research cited by Selzy, 29% of small companies most commonly send marketing emails weekly.
facts.quote: Small (29%) and mid-market (32%) companies most commonly send marketing emails weekly

facts.fact: According to Litmus research cited by Selzy, 32% of mid-market companies most commonly send marketing emails weekly.
facts.quote: Small (29%) and mid-market (32%) companies most commonly send marketing emails weekly

facts.fact: According to Litmus research cited by Selzy, 38% of enterprise businesses most commonly send emails several times per week.
facts.quote: enterprise businesses (38%) most commonly send emails several times per week.

facts.fact: In the MailerLite study cited by Selzy, email open rates stay relatively stable for monthly, weekly, and twice-weekly sends but drop when emails are sent daily.
facts.quote: It stays relatively stable when emails are sent monthly, weekly, or even twice a week. However, when emails are sent daily, open rates drop.

facts.fact: In the MailerLite study cited by Selzy, click-through rate generally improves as sending frequency increases, peaking at twice-weekly emails.
facts.quote: it generally improves as sending frequency increases, peaking at twice-weekly emails.

facts.fact: In the MailerLite study cited by Selzy, regular weekly or twice-weekly sending is associated with a lower unsubscribe rate, while very infrequent or inconsistent emailing is linked to higher unsubscribe rates.
facts.quote: By contrast, regular weekly or twice-weekly sending means a lower unsubscribe rate.

facts.fact: According to a Databox study cited by Selzy, most marketers report the best engagement on Tuesday emails.
facts.quote: most marketers report the best engagement on Tuesday emails
